sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Rails API mode strips the view layer and middleware unnecessary for JSON APIs, giving you a lighter ActionController::API base class instead of ActionController::Base. Interviewers at API-first Rails shops probe the serialization decision hard — Jbuilder uses templates (slow but flexible), ActiveModelSerializer follows conventions (well-established but slow for large collections), jsonapi-serializer (formerly fast_jsonapi from Netflix) is the fastest option, and Alba is a newer performant alternative. This page covers the api-only setup, CORS with rack-cors, the serialization comparison and when to use each, API versioning strategies (URL namespace is the most common), pagination with Pagy (faster than Kaminari), and rate limiting with Rack::Attack.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: api-only-setup, serialization-options, versioning-pagination, rate-limiting. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
